answer: An orchard yields only what was planted, so credit is tracked per tree. An identity earns standing only from work countersigned by two holders outside its own rows, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate tenders instead of one crew. Each added tree is priced by position: the k-th claim an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated witnesses. A crystal audit replays a random tree each epoch and voids the whole orchard on failure. Saffron marks each sealed claim, and marks cannot be transferred or re-dated.
